    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\t\t\t\t(pin power_out line (at 0 0 90) (length 0)\n")
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\t\t\t\t\t(name \"pwr\" " + font_effects + b")\n")
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\t\t\t\t\t(number \"1\" " + font_effects + b")\n\t\t\t\t)\n\t\t\t)\n")
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\t\t\t(embedded_fonts no)\n\t\t)\n")


public func pin_angle(side: shape_mod.Side) -> int:
    if side == shape_mod.Side.left:
        return 0
    if side == shape_mod.Side.right:
        return 180
    if side == shape_mod.Side.top:
        return 270
    return 90


func pin_point(p: Part, pin: shape_mod.Pin) -> int[]:
    return [p.x + pin.x, p.y - pin.y]


public func label_point(x: int, y: int, side: shape_mod.Side, reach: int) -> int[]:
    if side == shape_mod.Side.left:
        return [x - reach, y]
    if side == shape_mod.Side.right:
        return [x + reach, y]
    if side == shape_mod.Side.top:
        return [x, y - reach]
    return [x, y + reach]


public func stub_reach(u: shape_mod.ShapeUnit, i: int) -> int:
    return stub_len + shape_mod.stub_extra(u, i)


public func label_angle(side: shape_mod.Side) -> int:
    if side == shape_mod.Side.left:
        return 180
    if side == shape_mod.Side.right:
        return 0
    if side == shape_mod.Side.top:
        return 90
    return 270


public func label_justify(side: shape_mod.Side) -> bytes:
    if side == shape_mod.Side.left or side == shape_mod.Side.bottom:
        return b"right"
    return b"left"


public func rail_angle(side: shape_mod.Side) -> int:
    if side == shape_mod.Side.bottom:
        return 0
    if side == shape_mod.Side.right:
        return 90
    if side == shape_mod.Side.top:
        return 180
    return 270


func placed_symbol(mut w: byte_builder.Builder, doc: Doc, p: Part):
    mut s = doc.shapes[p.shape].copy()
    mut u = s.units[p.unit].copy()
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\t(symbol (lib_id \"" + lib_prefix + s.lib_name + b"\") ")
    at(mut w, p.x, p.y, p.banked.unwrap_or(0))
    byte_builder.append_text(mut w, " (unit " + str(u.number) + ")\n\t\t(exclude_from_sim no)\n")
    mut bom = b"yes"
    mut dnp = b"no"
    if p.id.dnp:
        bom = b"no"
        dnp = b"yes"
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\t\t(in_bom " + bom + b")\n\t\t(on_board yes)\n\t\t(dnp " + dnp + b")\n")
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\t\t(uuid \"" + p.id.uuid + b"\")\n")
    named_props(mut w, p, u)
    hidden_prop(mut w, b"Footprint", p.id.footprint, p.x, p.y)
    extra_props(mut w, p, u)
    instances(mut w, doc.sheet, p.id.ref, u.number)


func named_props(mut w: byte_builder.Builder, p: Part, u: shape_mod.ShapeUnit):
    mut ref_at = text_anchor(p, u, -1)
    mut val_at = text_anchor(p, u, 1)
    mut angle = 0
    mut just = b""
    if p.banked is not None:
        angle = 90
        just = b" (justify left)"
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\t\t(property \"Reference\" ")
    str_(mut w, p.id.ref)
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b" ")
    at(mut w, ref_at[0], ref_at[1], angle)
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b" (effects (font (size 1.27 1.27))" + just + b"))\n")
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\t\t(property \"Value\" ")
    str_(mut w, p.id.value)
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b" ")
    at(mut w, val_at[0], val_at[1], angle)
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b" (effects (font (size 1.27 1.27))" + just + b"))\n")


func text_anchor(p: Part, u: shape_mod.ShapeUnit, dir: int) -> int[]:
    if p.banked is not None:
        return [p.x + banked_text_dx, p.y + dir * shape_mod.grid]
    return [p.x, p.y + dir * field_reach(p, u)]


func field_reach(p: Part, u: shape_mod.ShapeUnit) -> int:
    mut span = 0
    for i in range(len(u.pins)):
        mut pin = u.pins[i].copy()
        if pin.side == shape_mod.Side.left or pin.side == shape_mod.Side.right:
            continue
        mut net = b""
        if i < len(p.nets):
            net = p.nets[i].copy()
        span = max(span, shape_mod.stub_extra(u, i) + label_span(net))
    return u.half_h + shape_mod.max_reach(u) + stub_len + span + shape_mod.pitch


func instances(mut w: byte_builder.Builder, s: Sheet, ref: bytes, unit: int):
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\t\t(instances\n\t\t\t(project ")
    str_(mut w, s.design)
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\n\t\t\t\t(path ")
    str_(mut w, instance_path(s))
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\n\t\t\t\t\t(reference ")
    str_(mut w, ref)
    byte_builder.append_text(mut w, ") (unit " + str(unit) + ")\n\t\t\t\t)\n\t\t\t)\n\t\t)\n\t)\n")


func hidden_prop(mut w: byte_builder.Builder, name: bytes, value: bytes, x: int, y: int):
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\t\t(property ")
    str_(mut w, name)
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b" ")
    str_(mut w, value)
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b" ")
    at(mut w, x, y, 0)
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b" " + hidden_font_effects + b")\n")


func extra_props(mut w: byte_builder.Builder, p: Part, u: shape_mod.ShapeUnit):
    mut datasheet = b""
    for prop in p.id.properties:
        if prop.key == b"datasheet":
            datasheet = prop.value.copy()
    hidden_prop(mut w, b"Datasheet", datasheet, p.x, p.y)
    mut shown = shown_mpn(p.id)
    for prop2 in p.id.properties:
        mut name = field_name(prop2.key)
        if name is None:
            continue
        if shown is not None and name == b"MPN":
            continue
        hidden_prop(mut w, name, prop2.value, p.x, p.y)
    if shown is None:
        return
    mut pt = mpn_anchor(p, u)
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\t\t(property \"MPN\" ")
    str_(mut w, shown)
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b" ")
    mut angle = 0
    if p.banked is not None:
        angle = 90
    at(mut w, pt[0], pt[1], angle)
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b" " + font_effects + b")\n")


func mpn_anchor(p: Part, u: shape_mod.ShapeUnit) -> int[]:
    mut value = text_anchor(p, u, 1)
    return [value[0], value[1] + mpn_drop]


func field_name(key: bytes) -> bytes?:
    if key == b"mpn":
        return Some(b"MPN")
    if key == b"manufacturer":
        return Some(b"Manufacturer")
    if key == b"datasheet" or key == b"footprint" or key == b"value" or len(key) == 0:
        return None
    return Some(key.copy())


func connections(mut w: byte_builder.Builder, doc: Doc, p: Part):
    if p.banked is not None:
        return
    mut u = doc.shapes[p.shape].units[p.unit].copy()
    for i in range(len(u.pins)):
        mut pin = u.pins[i].copy()
        mut net = b""
        if i < len(p.nets):
            net = p.nets[i].copy()
        mut pt = pin_point(p, pin)
        if len(net) == 0:
            byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\t(no_connect ")
            at2(mut w, pt)
            byte_builder.append(mut w, b" (uuid \"" + pin_uuid(doc.sheet.design, b"nc", p.id.ref, pin.pad) + b"\"))\n")
            continue
        mut lp = label_point(pt[0], pt[1], pin.side, stub_reach(u, i))
        wire(mut w, doc.sheet.design, pt, lp, pin_key(p.id.ref, pin.pad))
        if is_rail_pin(doc.power.pins, lp) or is_wired(doc.wiring.no_label, lp):
            continue
        global_label(mut w, net, pin_uuid(doc.sheet.design, b"label", p.id.ref, pin.pad), pin.side, lp)


func is_rail_pin(pins: RailPin[], pt: int[]) -> bool:
    for rp in pins:
        if rp.x == pt[0] and rp.y == pt[1]:
            return True
    return False


func is_wired(no_label: wire_mod.Point[], pt: int[]) -> bool:
    for p in no_label:
        if p.x == pt[0] and p.y == pt[1]:
            return True
    return False


func routed_wire(mut w: byte_builder.Builder, design: bytes, path: wire_mod.Path):
    for i in range(len(path.pts) - 1):
        mut a = path.pts[i]
        mut b = path.pts[i + 1]
        mut key = path.key + b"#" + str(i).encode()
        wire(mut w, design, [a.x, a.y], [b.x, b.y], key)


func junction(mut w: byte_builder.Builder, design: bytes, pt: wire_mod.Point):
    mut path = (str(pt.x) + "," + str(pt.y)).encode()
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\t(junction ")
    at2(mut w, [pt.x, pt.y])
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b" (diameter 0) (color 0 0 0 0)\n")
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\t\t(uuid \"" + element_uuid(design, b"junc", path) + b"\")\n\t)\n")


func wire(mut w: byte_builder.Builder, design: bytes, from_: int[], to: int[], key: bytes):
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\t(wire (pts ")
    at2xy(mut w, from_)
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b" ")
    at2xy(mut w, to)
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b")\n\t\t(stroke (width 0) (type default))\n\t\t(uuid \"" + element_uuid(design, b"wire", key) + b"\")\n\t)\n")


func global_label(mut w: byte_builder.Builder, net: bytes, uuid: bytes, side: shape_mod.Side, pt: int[]):
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\t(global_label ")
    str_(mut w, net)
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b" (shape bidirectional) ")
    at(mut w, pt[0], pt[1], label_angle(side))
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\n\t\t(fields_autoplaced yes)\n\t\t(effects (font (size 1.27 1.27)) (justify ")
    byte_builder.append(mut w, label_justify(side))
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"))\n\t\t(uuid \"" + uuid + b"\")\n\t)\n")


func rail_instance(mut w: byte_builder.Builder, doc: Doc, rp: RailPin):
    mut rail = doc.power.rails[rp.rail].copy()
    power_instance(mut w, doc.sheet, PowerPlacement(lib_name=rail.lib_name.copy(), value=rail.net.copy(), ref=rp.ref.copy(), uuid=rp.uuid.copy(), x=rp.x, y=rp.y, angle=rp.angle))


func flag_instance(mut w: byte_builder.Builder, doc: Doc, f: Flag):
    power_instance(mut w, doc.sheet, PowerPlacement(lib_name=flag_lib_name, value=flag_lib_name, ref=f.ref.copy(), uuid=f.uuid.copy(), x=f.x, y=f.y - stub_len, angle=0))
    wire(mut w, doc.sheet.design, [f.x, f.y - stub_len], [f.x, f.y], f.ref)
    mut uuid = pin_uuid(doc.sheet.design, b"label", f.ref, b"")
    global_label(mut w, f.net, uuid, shape_mod.Side.bottom, [f.x, f.y])


# Private in Zig; public for the bodyDir counterpart.
public record PowerPlacement:
    lib_name: bytes
    value: bytes
    ref: bytes
    uuid: bytes
    x: int
    y: int
    angle: int


func power_instance(mut w: byte_builder.Builder, s: Sheet, pp: PowerPlacement):
    mut dir = body_dir(pp)
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\t(symbol (lib_id \"" + lib_prefix + pp.lib_name + b"\") ")
    at(mut w, pp.x, pp.y, pp.angle)
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b" (unit 1)\n")
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\t\t(exclude_from_sim no)\n\t\t(in_bom no)\n\t\t(on_board no)\n\t\t(dnp no)\n")
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\t\t(uuid \"" + pp.uuid + b"\")\n")
    mut text_angle = 0
    if pp.angle == 90 or pp.angle == 270:
        text_angle = 90
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\t\t(property \"Reference\" ")
    str_(mut w, pp.ref)
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b" ")
    at(mut w, pp.x - dir[0] * text_reach, pp.y - dir[1] * text_reach, text_angle)
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b" " + hidden_font_effects + b")\n")
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\t\t(property \"Value\" ")
    str_(mut w, pp.value)
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b" ")
    at(mut w, pp.x + dir[0] * text_reach, pp.y + dir[1] * text_reach, text_angle)
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b" " + font_effects + b")\n")
    instances(mut w, s, pp.ref, 1)


public func body_dir(pp: PowerPlacement) -> int[]:
    mut away = 1
    if pp.lib_name == flag_lib_name:
        away = -1
    mut angle = pp.angle % 360
    if angle == 90:
        return [away, 0]
    if angle == 180:
        return [0, -away]
    if angle == 270:
        return [-away, 0]
    return [0, away]


func child_sheet(mut w: byte_builder.Builder, doc: Doc, c: SheetRef):
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\t(sheet ")
    at2(mut w, [c.at.x, c.at.y])
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b" (size ")
    mm(mut w, c.at.w)
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b" ")
    mm(mut w, c.at.h)
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b")\n\t\t(exclude_from_sim no)\n\t\t(in_bom yes)\n\t\t(on_board yes)\n\t\t(dnp no)\n")
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\t\t(fields_autoplaced yes)\n\t\t(stroke (width 0.1524) (type solid))\n")
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\t\t(fill (color 0 0 0 0))\n\t\t(uuid \"" + c.uuid + b"\")\n")
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\t\t(property \"Sheetname\" ")
    str_(mut w, c.name)
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b" ")
    at(mut w, c.at.x, c.at.y - shape_mod.grid, 0)
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b" (effects (font (size 1.27 1.27)) (justify left bottom)))\n")
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\t\t(property \"Sheetfile\" ")
    str_(mut w, c.file)
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b" ")
    at(mut w, c.at.x, c.at.y + c.at.h + shape_mod.grid, 0)
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b" (effects (font (size 1.27 1.27)) (justify left top)))\n")
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\t\t(instances\n\t\t\t(project ")
    str_(mut w, doc.sheet.design)
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\n\t\t\t\t(path ")
    str_(mut w, instance_path(doc.sheet))
    byte_builder.append_text(mut w, "\n\t\t\t\t\t(page \"" + str(c.page) + "\")\n\t\t\t\t)\n\t\t\t)\n\t\t)\n\t)\n")


func pin_key(ref: bytes, pad: bytes) -> bytes:
    return ref + b":" + pad


func pin_uuid(design: bytes, kind: bytes, ref: bytes, pad: bytes) -> bytes:
    return element_uuid(design, kind, pin_key(ref, pad))


func at2(mut w: byte_builder.Builder, pt: int[]):
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"(at ")
    mm(mut w, pt[0])
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b" ")
    mm(mut w, pt[1])
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b")")


func at2xy(mut w: byte_builder.Builder, pt: int[]):
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"(xy ")
    mm(mut w, pt[0])
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b" ")
    mm(mut w, pt[1])
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b")")


func caption(mut w: byte_builder.Builder, design: bytes, c: Caption, path: bytes):
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\t(text ")
    str_(mut w, c.text)
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\n\t\t(exclude_from_sim no)\n\t\t")
    at(mut w, c.x, c.y, 0)
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\n\t\t(effects (font (size ")
    mm(mut w, c.size)
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b" ")
    mm(mut w, c.size)
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b")) (justify left bottom))\n\t\t(uuid \"")
    byte_builder.append(mut w, element_uuid(design, b"cap", path) + b"\")\n\t)\n")

import kicad_sch_emit as m
import kicad_sch_shape as shape

# test "kicad-sch: mm prints exact hundredths and str escapes"
public func test_kicad_sch_mm_prints_exact_hundredths_and_str_escapes() -> bool:
    mut out = byte_builder.create()
    m.mm(mut out, 6350)
    byte_builder.append(mut out, b" ")
    m.mm(mut out, -1524)
    byte_builder.append(mut out, b" ")
    m.mm(mut out, 6858)
    byte_builder.append(mut out, b" ")
    m.mm(mut out, 0)
    byte_builder.append(mut out, b" ")
    m.str_(mut out, b"a\"b\\c")
    assert byte_builder.finish(out) == b"63.5 -15.24 68.58 0 \"a\\\"b\\\\c\""
    return True


# test "kicad-sch: mm4 prints ten-thousandths of a millimetre exactly"
public func test_kicad_sch_mm4_prints_ten_thousandths_of_a_millimetre_exactly() -> bool:
    mut out = byte_builder.create()
    mut nums = [25400, -1270, 8467, 0, 1000000, 1524]
    for i in range(len(nums)):
        if i > 0:
            byte_builder.append(mut out, b" ")
        m.mm4(mut out, nums[i])
    assert byte_builder.finish(out) == b"2.54 -0.127 0.8467 0 100 0.1524"
    return True


# test "kicad-sch: label angle and justification mirror the pin side"
public func test_kicad_sch_label_angle_and_justification_mirror_the_pin_side() -> bool:
    assert m.label_angle(shape.Side.left) == 180 and m.label_angle(shape.Side.right) == 0
    assert m.label_justify(shape.Side.left) == b"right" and m.label_justify(shape.Side.right) == b"left"
    assert m.label_justify(shape.Side.top) == b"left" and m.label_justify(shape.Side.bottom) == b"right"
    assert m.pin_angle(shape.Side.left) == 0 and m.pin_angle(shape.Side.right) == 180
    assert m.rail_angle(shape.Side.bottom) == 0 and m.rail_angle(shape.Side.right) == 90
    assert m.rail_angle(shape.Side.top) == 180 and m.rail_angle(shape.Side.left) == 270
    return True


# test "kicad-sch: a rail symbol's text hangs with its body and a flag's the other way"
public func test_kicad_sch_a_rail_symbol_s_text_hangs_with_its_body_and_a_flag_s_the_other_way() -> bool:
    mut rail = m.PowerPlacement(lib_name=b"PWR_GND", value=b"GND", ref=b"#PWR01", uuid=b"u", x=0, y=0, angle=0)
    assert m.body_dir(rail) == [0, 1]
    mut left = rail.copy()
    left.angle = 270
    assert m.body_dir(left) == [-1, 0]
    mut right = rail.copy()
    right.angle = 90
    assert m.body_dir(right) == [1, 0]
    mut flag = rail.copy()
    flag.lib_name = m.flag_lib_name
    assert m.body_dir(flag) == [0, -1]
    return True


# test "kicad-sch: labelSpan budgets what KiCad actually draws"
public func test_kicad_sch_labelspan_budgets_what_kicad_actually_draws() -> bool:
    assert m.label_span(b"") == 0
    assert m.label_span(b"GND") > 3 * shape.grid
    assert m.label_span(b"VDDCORE") >= 7 * shape.grid
    assert m.label_span(b"VDDCOREX") > m.label_span(b"VDDCORE")
    return True


# test "kicad-sch: pin text shrinks on a fine-pitch edge and stays full size elsewhere"
public func test_kicad_sch_pin_text_shrinks_on_a_fine_pitch_edge_and_stays_full_size_elsewhere() -> bool:
    mut roomy = [shape.Pin(pad=b"1", name=b"A", side=shape.Side.left, x=-1270, y=254), shape.Pin(pad=b"2", name=b"B", side=shape.Side.left, x=-1270, y=0), shape.Pin(pad=b"3", name=b"C", side=shape.Side.right, x=1270, y=0)]
    mut wide = shape.ShapeUnit(number=1, title=b"", pins=roomy, half_w=1016, half_h=508, graphics=[], stubs=[])
    assert m.pin_text_size(wide, 0) == 127 and m.pin_text_size(wide, 2) == 127
    mut want: int? = Some(254)
    assert m.edge_spacing(wide, 0) == want and m.edge_spacing(wide, 2) is None
    mut tight = [shape.Pin(pad=b"1", name=b"A", side=shape.Side.left, x=-1270, y=127), shape.Pin(pad=b"2", name=b"B", side=shape.Side.left, x=-1270, y=0)]
    mut dense = shape.ShapeUnit(number=1, title=b"", pins=tight, half_w=1016, half_h=508, graphics=[], stubs=[])
    mut size = m.pin_text_size(dense, 0)
    assert size < 127 and size >= 50 and size % 10 == 0
    assert size + size // 5 < 127
    return True


# test "kicad-sch: the instance path gains a sheet segment on a child file"
public func test_kicad_sch_the_instance_path_gains_a_sheet_segment_on_a_child_file() -> bool:
    mut root = m.Sheet(design=b"d", title=b"", root_uuid=b"R", sheet_uuid=b"R", page_w=1, page_h=1, is_root=True)
    assert m.instance_path(root) == b"/R"
    mut child = root
    child.sheet_uuid = b"S"
    child.is_root = False
    assert m.instance_path(child) == b"/R/S"
    return True

    mut sym_table = b"".join([b"(sym_lib_table\n\t(version 7)\n\t(lib (name \"netlisp\")(type \"KiCad\")", b"(uri \"${KIPRJMOD}/netlisp.kicad_sym\")(options \"\")", b"(descr \"Symbols exported by netlisp\"))\n)\n"])
    mut fp_table = b"".join([b"(fp_lib_table\n\t(version 7)\n\t(lib (name \"footprints\")(type \"KiCad\")", b"(uri \"${KIPRJMOD}/footprints.pretty\")(options \"\")", b"(descr \"Footprints exported by netlisp export-kicad\"))\n)\n"])
    return [Sidecar(name=sym_lib_table_file, bytes=sym_table), Sidecar(name=fp_lib_table_file, bytes=fp_table), Sidecar(name=project_name.copy(), bytes=project_file(project_name)), Sidecar(name=sym_lib_file, bytes=emit.library_file(shapes, rails))]


# Private in Zig; public for the sibling hostile-name test.
public func project_file(project_name: bytes) -> bytes:
    mut out = byte_builder.create()
    byte_builder.append(mut out, b"{\n  \"board\": {},\n  \"libraries\": {\n")
    byte_builder.append(mut out, b"    \"pinned_footprint_libs\": [],\n    \"pinned_symbol_libs\": []\n  },\n")
    byte_builder.append(mut out, b"  \"meta\": {\n    \"filename\": ")
    json_writer.write_string(mut out, project_name)
    byte_builder.append(mut out, b",\n    \"version\": 1\n  },\n")
    byte_builder.append(mut out, b"  \"net_settings\": {},\n  \"pcbnew\": {},\n  \"schematic\": {},\n")
    byte_builder.append(mut out, b"  \"sheets\": [],\n  \"text_variables\": {}\n}\n")
    return byte_builder.finish(out)

import kicad_sch_project as m
import kicad_sch_shape as shape
import kicad_sch_emit as emit
import json
import support_strs as strs

func fixture_shapes() -> shape.Shape[]:
    mut units = [shape.ShapeUnit(number=1, title=b"", pins=[], half_w=254, half_h=254, graphics=[], stubs=[])]
    return [shape.Shape(lib_name=b"demo-part", units=units)]


func project_json(data: bytes) -> json.Json:
    match json.loads(strs.text(data)):
        case Ok(document):
            return document
        case Err(_):
            assert False, "invalid project JSON"
            return json.null_value()


# test "kicad-sch: the sidecar set names the four project files"
public func test_kicad_sch_the_sidecar_set_names_the_four_project_files() -> bool:
    mut files = m.sidecars(b"demo", fixture_shapes(), [emit.Rail(lib_name=b"PWR_GND", net=b"GND")])
    assert len(files) == 4
    assert [for f in files yield f.name.copy()] == [b"sym-lib-table", b"fp-lib-table", b"demo.kicad_pro", b"netlisp.kicad_sym"]
    assert files[0].bytes.find(b"(name \"netlisp\")") >= 0
    assert files[1].bytes.find(b"(name \"footprints\")") >= 0
    assert files[0].bytes.find(b"${KIPRJMOD}/netlisp.kicad_sym") >= 0
    assert files[1].bytes.find(b"${KIPRJMOD}/footprints.pretty") >= 0
    assert files[2].bytes.find(b"\"demo.kicad_pro\"") >= 0
    assert json.get(project_json(files[2].bytes), "meta") is not None
    assert files[3].bytes.find(b"(kicad_symbol_lib") >= 0
    assert files[3].bytes.find(b"(symbol \"PWR_FLAG\"") >= 0
    return True


# test "kicad-sch: the symbol library drops the lib_id prefix"
public func test_kicad_sch_the_symbol_library_drops_the_lib_id_prefix() -> bool:
    mut shapes = fixture_shapes()
    mut rails = [emit.Rail(lib_name=b"PWR_GND", net=b"GND")]
    mut text = emit.library_file(shapes, rails)
    assert text.startswith(b"(kicad_symbol_lib")
    assert text.find(b"(symbol \"demo-part\"") >= 0
    assert text.find(b"(symbol \"PWR_GND\"") >= 0
    assert text.find(b"netlisp:") < 0
    assert text.find(b"(symbol \"PWR_FLAG\"") >= 0
    return True


# test "kicad-sch: the project file escapes a hostile design name"
public func test_kicad_sch_the_project_file_escapes_a_hostile_design_name() -> bool:
    mut files = m.sidecars(b"od\"d\\n<a>me\x01", [], [])
    assert files[2].bytes.find(b"<a>") >= 0
    mut document = project_json(files[2].bytes)
    match json.get(document, "meta"):
        case Some(meta):
            match json.get(meta, "filename"):
                case Some(filename):
                    assert json.as_str(filename) == Some("od\"d\\n<a>me\x01.kicad_pro")
                case None:
                    assert False, "missing project filename"
        case None:
            assert False, "missing project meta"
    return True

import kicad_sch_stagger as m
import kicad_sch_shape as shape
import kicad_sch_emit as emit

func left_pin(pad: bytes, y: int) -> shape.Pin:
    return shape.Pin(pad=pad.copy(), name=pad.copy(), side=shape.Side.left, x=-1270, y=y)


func unit_of(pins: shape.Pin[]) -> shape.ShapeUnit:
    return shape.ShapeUnit(number=1, title=b"", pins=pins.copy(), half_w=1016, half_h=2540, graphics=[], stubs=[])


func shape_of(pins: shape.Pin[]) -> shape.Shape:
    return shape.Shape(lib_name=b"x", units=[unit_of(pins)])


# test "kicad-sch: a crowded edge spreads into two stub columns and a roomy one does not"
public func test_kicad_sch_a_crowded_edge_spreads_into_two_stub_columns_and_a_roomy_one_does_not() -> bool:
    mut nets: dict[str, bytes] = {"1": b"AAA", "2": b"BBB", "3": b"CCC", "4": b"DDD"}
    mut tight = [left_pin(b"1", 381), left_pin(b"2", 254), left_pin(b"3", 127), left_pin(b"4", 0)]
    mut spread = m.spread(shape_of(tight), Some(nets.copy()))
    mut stubs = spread.units[0].stubs.copy()
    assert len(stubs) == 4 and stubs[0] == 0 and stubs[2] == 0
    assert stubs[1] > emit.label_span(b"AAA") and stubs[1] == stubs[3]
    mut roomy = [left_pin(b"1", 762), left_pin(b"2", 508), left_pin(b"3", 254), left_pin(b"4", 0)]
    mut kept = m.spread(shape_of(roomy), Some(nets.copy()))
    assert len(kept.units[0].stubs) == 0 and shape.stub_extra(kept.units[0], 1) == 0
    return True


# test "kicad-sch: a same-net run shares one column and holds its neighbours apart"
public func test_kicad_sch_a_same_net_run_shares_one_column_and_holds_its_neighbours_apart() -> bool:
    mut pins = [left_pin(b"1", 508), left_pin(b"2", 381), left_pin(b"3", 254), left_pin(b"4", 127), left_pin(b"5", 0)]
    mut nets: dict[str, bytes] = {"1": b"GND", "2": b"GND", "3": b"GND", "4": b"SDA", "5": b"SCL"}
    mut stubs = m.spread(shape_of(pins), Some(nets.copy())).units[0].stubs.copy()
    assert stubs[0] == stubs[1] and stubs[1] == stubs[2]
    assert stubs[0] == stubs[3] and stubs[4] > stubs[3]
    return True


# test "kicad-sch: spreading repeats exactly and skips unconnected pads"
public func test_kicad_sch_spreading_repeats_exactly_and_skips_unconnected_pads() -> bool:
    mut pins = [left_pin(b"1", 254), left_pin(b"2", 127), left_pin(b"3", 0)]
    mut nets: dict[str, bytes] = {"1": b"AAA", "3": b"CCC"}
    mut first = m.spread(shape_of(pins), Some(nets.copy()))
    assert len(first.units[0].stubs) == 0
    nets["2"] = b"BBB"
    mut one = m.spread(shape_of(pins), Some(nets.copy()))
    mut two = m.spread(shape_of(pins), Some(nets.copy()))
    assert one.units[0].stubs == two.units[0].stubs
    assert one.units[0].stubs[0] == 0 and one.units[0].stubs[1] > 0 and one.units[0].stubs[2] == 0
    return True


# test "kicad-sch: spreading needs the net map and leaves a shape without one alone"
public func test_kicad_sch_spreading_needs_the_net_map_and_leaves_a_shape_without_one_alone() -> bool:
    mut pins = [left_pin(b"1", 127), left_pin(b"2", 0)]
    mut out = m.spread(shape_of(pins), None)
    assert len(out.units[0].stubs) == 0
    return True


# test "kicad-sch: a spread unit keeps every pin endpoint, side and body it was given"
public func test_kicad_sch_a_spread_unit_keeps_every_pin_endpoint_side_and_body_it_was_given() -> bool:
    mut pins = [left_pin(b"1", 254), left_pin(b"2", 127), left_pin(b"3", 0)]
    mut nets: dict[str, bytes] = {"1": b"AAA", "2": b"BBB", "3": b"CCC"}
    mut before = unit_of(pins)
    mut after = m.spread(shape.Shape(lib_name=b"x", units=[before.copy()], vendor=True), Some(nets.copy())).units[0].copy()
    assert len(after.stubs) == len(pins) and after.stubs[1] > 0
    assert before.pins == after.pins and before.half_w == after.half_w and before.half_h == after.half_h
    assert len(before.graphics) == len(after.graphics)
    return True

import kicad_sym_reader as reader
import infra_fs as fsx
import infra_log as log
import support_strs as strs

# Vendor files are indexed in bytewise filename order. The first registration
# wins; missing directories and unreadable libraries cost only vendor coverage.
public const sources_subdir: str = "lib/sources"


public const suffix: str = ".kicad_sym"


const max_vendor_symbol_bytes: int = 4194304


const max_name_len: int = 128


public record Library:
    by_name: dict[str, reader.Symbol]
    files: int = 0


public func library_find(self: Library, name: bytes) -> reader.Symbol?:
    if len(name) == 0 or len(name) > max_name_len:
        return None
    mut key = normalize(name)
    if key in self.by_name:
        return Some(self.by_name[key].copy())
    return None


public func load(fs: Filesystem, err: Stream, project_dir: str) -> Library:
    mut lib = Library(by_name={})
    mut dir_path = project_dir + "/" + sources_subdir
    mut files = list_sources(fs, dir_path)
    files.sort()
    for name in files:
        index_file(fs, err, mut lib, dir_path, name)
    return lib


func list_sources(fs: Filesystem, dir_path: str) -> str[]:
    mut out: str[] = []
    match fsx.list_dir(fs, dir_path):
        case Err(_):
            return out
        case Ok(names):
            for name in names:
                # No entry kind is available (D4). A directory with this
                # suffix cannot read_file and is discarded by index_file.
                if name.endswith(suffix):
                    out.append(name.copy())
    return out


func index_file(fs: Filesystem, err: Stream, mut lib: Library, dir_path: str, file: str):
    mut path = dir_path + "/" + file
    mut src: bytes = b""
    match fsx.read_file_alloc(fs, path, max_vendor_symbol_bytes):
        case Err(_):
            return
        case Ok(data):
            src = data
    mut syms: reader.Symbol[] = []
    match reader.parse_library(src):
        case Err(e):
            log.warn(err, ("export-kicad-sch: vendor symbol library " + file + " is unreadable (" + e + ")").encode())
            return
        case Ok(parsed):
            syms = parsed
    if len(syms) == 0:
        return
    lib.files += 1
    for sym in syms:
        register(mut lib, sym.name, sym)
    register(mut lib, file[0:len(file) - len(suffix)].encode(), syms[0])


func register(mut lib: Library, name: bytes, sym: reader.Symbol):
    if len(name) == 0 or len(name) > max_name_len:
        return
    mut key = normalize(name)
    if key not in lib.by_name:
        lib.by_name[key] = sym.copy()


# Same part-name normalization as the footprint passthrough lookup.
func normalize(name: bytes) -> str:
    mut out: int[] = []
    for c in name:
        if c == 95:
            out.append(45)
        else:
            out.append(strs.to_lower(c))
    return strs.text(bytes(out))

import byte_builder

# Read caps belong to each lib/ file class. Raise these, never lower them:
# most callers swallow a failed read and quietly omit the missing part.
public const max_footprint_bytes: int = 1048576


public const max_lib_file_bytes: int = 1048576


public const retired_lib_file_cap_bytes: int = 262144


public func synth_pinout_source(name: bytes, min_bytes: int) -> bytes:
    mut w = byte_builder.create()
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"(pinout \"")
    byte_builder.append(mut w, name)
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"\"\n")
    mut size = len(name) + 11
    mut i = 1
    while size < min_bytes:
        mut line = ("  (pin " + str(i) + " \"PIN" + str(i) + "\" (alt \"ALT" + str(i) + "\" io))\n").encode()
        byte_builder.append(mut w, line)
        size += len(line)
        i += 1
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"  (pin LAST \"LASTFN\" (alt \"SENTINEL\" io))\n)\n")
    return byte_builder.finish(w)

# Port of zig/src/numeric.zig: safe float -> int narrowing. Zig's
# `checkedInt(comptime T, f)` is generic over the integer type; mylang has no
# comptime type parameter, so it is one range-checked core plus one typed
# wrapper per width the slice uses.
#
# The range check runs in float space before the conversion, and the upper
# bound is the EXCLUSIVE limit maxInt(T)+1 (a power of two, exact in f64 at
# every width).
import math

# Round `f` to the nearest integer (half away from zero, like Zig @round) and
# return it as a float, or None when `f` is non-finite or rounds outside
# [lo, hi_excl).
public func checked_round(f: float, lo: float, hi_excl: float) -> float?:
    if not math.is_finite(f):
        return None
    mut r = round(f)
    if r < lo or r >= hi_excl:
        return None
    return Some(r)


# Convert an already range-checked, integral float in [0, 2^64) to u64. mylang
# has no float -> u64 cast, so the upper half goes through int by subtracting
# 2^63 (exact in f64 there).
func float_to_u64(r: float) -> u64:
    if r < 9223372036854775808.0:
        return u64(int(r))
    return u64(int(r - 9223372036854775808.0)) + 9223372036854775808u64


public func checked_i64(f: float) -> int?:
    match checked_round(f, -9223372036854775808.0, 9223372036854775808.0):
        case Some(r):
            return Some(int(r))
        case None:
            return None


public func checked_u64(f: float) -> u64?:
    match checked_round(f, 0.0, 18446744073709551616.0):
        case Some(r):
            return Some(float_to_u64(r))
        case None:
            return None


public func checked_i32(f: float) -> i32?:
    match checked_round(f, -2147483648.0, 2147483648.0):
        case Some(r):
            return Some(i32(int(r)))
        case None:
            return None


public func checked_u32(f: float) -> u32?:
    match checked_round(f, 0.0, 4294967296.0):
        case Some(r):
            return Some(u32(int(r)))
        case None:
            return None


public func checked_i8(f: float) -> i8?:
    match checked_round(f, -128.0, 128.0):
        case Some(r):
            return Some(i8(int(r)))
        case None:
            return None


public func checked_u8(f: float) -> u8?:
    match checked_round(f, 0.0, 256.0):
        case Some(r):
            return Some(u8(int(r)))
        case None:
            return None


# Narrow `f` to a non-negative count/index (Zig usize), collapsing a non-finite
# or out-of-range value to 0.
public func to_count(f: float) -> u64:
    match checked_u64(f):
        case Some(v):
            return v
        case None:
            return 0u64

# test "checkedInt rejects NaN and infinities"
public func test_checkedint_rejects_nan_and_infinities() -> bool:
    assert numeric.checked_i64(nan()) is None, "nan"
    assert numeric.checked_i64(inf()) is None, "inf"
    assert numeric.checked_i64(-inf()) is None, "-inf"
    return True


# test "checkedInt rejects out-of-range and rounds in-range"
public func test_checkedint_rejects_out_of_range_and_rounds_in_range() -> bool:
    assert numeric.checked_u8(300.0) is None, "u8 300"
    assert numeric.checked_u8(-1.0) is None, "u8 -1"
    assert is_u32(numeric.checked_u32(220000.4), u32(220000)), "u32 220000.4"
    assert is_i64(numeric.checked_i64(-2.6), -3), "i64 -2.6"
    assert is_u32(numeric.checked_u32(0.0), u32(0)), "u32 0"
    # Zig @round is half away from zero.
    assert is_i64(numeric.checked_i64(2.5), 3), "2.5 rounds up"
    assert is_i64(numeric.checked_i64(-2.5), -3), "-2.5 rounds away from zero"
    assert is_i64(numeric.checked_i64(0.5), 1), "0.5 rounds up"
    return True


# test "checkedInt is exact at each type's maximum"
public func test_checkedint_is_exact_at_each_type_s_maximum() -> bool:
    # Narrow widths (value bits <= 53): maxInt is exactly representable in f64,
    # so the maximum itself converts and maxInt+1 is rejected.
    assert is_u8(numeric.checked_u8(255.0), u8(255)), "u8 max"
    assert numeric.checked_u8(256.0) is None, "u8 max+1"
    assert is_i8(numeric.checked_i8(127.0), i8(127)), "i8 max"
    assert numeric.checked_i8(128.0) is None, "i8 max+1"
    assert is_i8(numeric.checked_i8(-128.0), i8(-128)), "i8 min"
    assert numeric.checked_i8(-129.0) is None, "i8 min-1"
    assert is_u32(numeric.checked_u32(4294967295.0), u32(4294967295)), "u32 max"
    assert numeric.checked_u32(4294967296.0) is None, "u32 max+1"
    assert is_i32(numeric.checked_i32(2147483647.0), i32(2147483647)), "i32 max"
    assert numeric.checked_i32(2147483648.0) is None, "i32 max+1"
    # 64-bit: maxInt is NOT representable in f64. float(maxInt) rounds UP to
    # maxInt+1, so the exclusive bound must reject it.
    assert numeric.checked_i64(9223372036854775808.0) is None, "2^63"
    assert numeric.checked_u64(18446744073709551616.0) is None, "2^64"
    assert numeric.checked_i64(float(9223372036854775807)) is None, "float(maxInt(i64))"
    assert numeric.checked_u64(float(18446744073709551615u64)) is None, "float(maxInt(u64))"
    # The largest f64 strictly below each bound must still convert.
    assert is_i64(numeric.checked_i64(9223372036854774784.0), 9223372036854774784), "2^63 - 2^10"
    assert is_u64(numeric.checked_u64(18446744073709549568.0), 18446744073709549568u64), "2^64 - 2^11"
    # The low bound is exact at every width.
    assert is_i64(numeric.checked_i64(-9223372036854775808.0), -9223372036854775807 - 1), "-2^63"
    assert numeric.checked_i64(-9223372036854777856.0) is None, "next f64 below -2^63"
    assert numeric.checked_u64(-1.0) is None, "u64 -1"
    # usize bound (64-bit target): toCount rides the same bound.
    assert numeric.checked_u64(18446744073709551616.0) is None, "usize 2^64"
    assert is_u64(numeric.checked_u64(18446744073709549568.0), 18446744073709549568u64), "usize 2^64 - 2^11"
    assert numeric.to_count(18446744073709551616.0) == 0u64, "toCount 2^64"
    return True


# test "toCount collapses non-finite and negative to zero, rounds valid counts"
public func test_tocount_collapses_non_finite_and_negative_to_zero_rounds_valid_counts() -> bool:
    assert numeric.to_count(nan()) == 0u64, "nan"
    assert numeric.to_count(inf()) == 0u64, "inf"
    assert numeric.to_count(-4.0) == 0u64, "negative"
    assert numeric.to_count(6.6) == 7u64, "6.6"
    return True

# Port of zig/src/sexpr/parser.zig: recursive-descent S-expression parser with a
# hard nesting-depth cap. Checked ownership keeps independent node text slices.
#
# Differences from the Zig: no `OutOfMemory` error (an allocation failure traps
# in mylang) and no `freeNodes` (the runtime reclaims managed values).
import sexpr_ast as ast
import sexpr_tokenizer as tokenizer_mod

# 1 mil = 0.0254 mm (mylang has no float module constants, so a function).
func mil_to_mm() -> float:
    return 0.0254


# Maximum S-expression nesting depth (parse_list -> parse_node -> parse_list
# recurses once per open paren).
public const MAX_PARSE_DEPTH: int = 10000


public enum ParseError:
    unexpected_eof
    unexpected_rparen
    unexpected_character
    unterminated_string
    invalid_number
    too_deep


# Source-located explanation for a ParseError.
public record ParseDiagnostic:
    span: ast.Span
    message: str


public func new_diagnostic() -> ParseDiagnostic:
    return ParseDiagnostic(span=ast.span_zero(), message="")


# Human-readable message for each ParseError kind.
public func error_message(err: ParseError) -> str:
    match err:
        case ParseError.unexpected_eof:
            return "unexpected end of input — a '(' was never closed"
        case ParseError.unexpected_rparen:
            return "unexpected ')' — no matching '(' is open here"
        case ParseError.unexpected_character:
            return "unexpected character"
        case ParseError.unterminated_string:
            return "unterminated string — missing closing '\"'"
        case ParseError.invalid_number:
            return "invalid number literal"
        case ParseError.too_deep:
            return "s-expression nesting is too deep"


# The Zig error identity, distinct from the human-facing diagnostic text.
public func error_name(err: ParseError) -> str:
    match err:
        case ParseError.unexpected_eof:
            return "UnexpectedEof"
        case ParseError.unexpected_rparen:
            return "UnexpectedRparen"
        case ParseError.unexpected_character:
            return "UnexpectedCharacter"
        case ParseError.unterminated_string:
            return "UnterminatedString"
        case ParseError.invalid_number:
            return "InvalidNumber"
        case ParseError.too_deep:
            return "TooDeep"


func lex_error_to_parse(err: tokenizer_mod.LexError) -> ParseError:
    match err:
        case tokenizer_mod.LexError.unexpected_character:
            return ParseError.unexpected_character
        case tokenizer_mod.LexError.unterminated_string:
            return ParseError.unterminated_string


# Parse S-expression source into a list of top-level nodes, discarding any
# diagnostic.
public func parse(source: bytes) -> Result[ast.Node[], ParseError]:
    mut diag = new_diagnostic()
    return parse_diag(source, mut diag)


# Parse, writing a source-located diagnostic into `diag` on failure. On success
# `diag` is left untouched.
public func parse_diag(source: bytes, mut diag: ParseDiagnostic) -> Result[ast.Node[], ParseError]:
    match parse_inner(source, mut diag):
        case Ok(nodes):
            return Ok(nodes)
        case Err(err):
            if len(diag.message) == 0:
                diag.message = error_message(err)
            return Err(err)


func parse_inner(source: bytes, mut diag: ParseDiagnostic) -> Result[ast.Node[], ParseError]:
    mut tok = tokenizer_mod.tokenizer_init(source)
    mut nodes: ast.Node[] = []
    while True:
        mut token = try next_token(mut tok, mut diag)
        if token.tag == tokenizer_mod.TokenTag.eof:
            break
        mut node = try parse_node(mut tok, token, 0, mut diag)
        nodes.append(node)
    return Ok(nodes)


# Advance the tokenizer, capturing the failing byte's span into `diag` when the
# lexer rejects a character or an unterminated string.
func next_token(mut tok: tokenizer_mod.Tokenizer, mut diag: ParseDiagnostic) -> Result[tokenizer_mod.Token, ParseError]:
    match tokenizer_mod.next(mut tok):
        case Ok(token):
            return Ok(token)
        case Err(err):
            mut perr = lex_error_to_parse(err)
            diag.span = tok.cur.error_span
            diag.message = error_message(perr)
            return Err(perr)


# Record `span` + the message for `err` into `diag`, so a parser-level
# rejection reports where it happened.
func fail (mut diag: ParseDiagnostic, span: ast.Span, err: ParseError) -> ParseError:
    diag.span = span
    diag.message = error_message(err)
    return err


func parse_node(mut tok: tokenizer_mod.Tokenizer, token: tokenizer_mod.Token, depth: int, mut diag: ParseDiagnostic) -> Result[ast.Node, ParseError]:
    match token.tag:
        case tokenizer_mod.TokenTag.lparen:
            return parse_list(mut tok, token.span, depth, mut diag)
        case tokenizer_mod.TokenTag.rparen:
            return Err(fail (mut diag, token.span, ParseError.unexpected_rparen))
        case tokenizer_mod.TokenTag.atom:
            return Ok(ast.node_atom(token.span, token.text))
        case tokenizer_mod.TokenTag.string:
            return Ok(ast.node_string(token.span, token.text))
        case tokenizer_mod.TokenTag.eof:
            return Err(fail (mut diag, token.span, ParseError.unexpected_eof))
        case _:
            return parse_number_node(tok, token, mut diag)


# Parse a numeric token (int/float/si_val/unit_val) into its AST node, applying
# the SI scale suffix or the mm/mil dimension conversion.
func parse_number_node(tok: tokenizer_mod.Tokenizer, token: tokenizer_mod.Token, mut diag: ParseDiagnostic) -> Result[ast.Node, ParseError]:
    match token.tag:
        case tokenizer_mod.TokenTag.int:
            match token.text.parse_int():
                case Some(val):
                    return Ok(ast.node_int(token.span, val))
                case None:
                    return Err(fail (mut diag, token.span, ParseError.invalid_number))
        case tokenizer_mod.TokenTag.float:
            match token.text.parse_float():
                case Some(val):
                    return Ok(ast.node_float(token.span, val))
                case None:
                    return Err(fail (mut diag, token.span, ParseError.invalid_number))
        case tokenizer_mod.TokenTag.si_val:
            match parse_si_value(token.text):
                case Some(val):
                    # Keep the source spelling so a renderer can write `100nF`
                    # back instead of `0.0000001`.
                    return Ok(ast.node_suffixed_float(token.span, val, token.text))
                case None:
                    return Err(fail (mut diag, token.span, ParseError.invalid_number))
        case tokenizer_mod.TokenTag.unit_val:
            match token.text.parse_float():
                case Some(val):
                    mut after_pos = token.span.offset + len(token.text)
                    mut mm_value = val
                    if after_pos + 2 < len(tok.source) and tok.source[after_pos] == ord("m") and tok.source[after_pos + 1] == ord("i") and tok.source[after_pos + 2] == ord("l"):
                        mm_value = val * mil_to_mm()
                    return Ok(ast.node_unit_val(token.span, mm_value))
                case None:
                    return Err(fail (mut diag, token.span, ParseError.invalid_number))
        case _:
            return Err(fail (mut diag, token.span, ParseError.invalid_number))


# Parse an SI-scaled literal token (`220k`, `100nF`, `3.3V`, `10%`) into its
# numeric value. None when the text has no parsable numeric prefix.
func parse_si_value(text: bytes) -> float?:
    mut num_end = 0
    while num_end < len(text):
        mut c = text[num_end]
        mut numeric = (c >= ord("0") and c <= ord("9")) or c == ord(".") or (c == ord("-") and num_end == 0)
        if not numeric:
            break
        num_end += 1
    if num_end == 0 or num_end == len(text):
        return None
    match text[0:num_end].parse_float():
        case None:
            return None
        case Some(base):
            mut scale = 1.0
            for s in tokenizer_mod.si_scales():
                if s.letter == text[num_end]:
                    scale = s.multiplier
                    break
            return Some(base * scale)


func parse_list(mut tok: tokenizer_mod.Tokenizer, open_span: ast.Span, depth: int, mut diag: ParseDiagnostic) -> Result[ast.Node, ParseError]:
    if depth >= MAX_PARSE_DEPTH:
        return Err(fail (mut diag, open_span, ParseError.too_deep))
    mut children: ast.Node[] = []
    while True:
        mut token = try next_token(mut tok, mut diag)
        # Point an unterminated list at the '(' that was never closed.
        if token.tag == tokenizer_mod.TokenTag.eof:
            return Err(fail (mut diag, open_span, ParseError.unexpected_eof))
        if token.tag == tokenizer_mod.TokenTag.rparen:
            break
        mut child = try parse_node(mut tok, token, depth + 1, mut diag)
        children.append(child)
    return Ok(ast.node_list(open_span, children))

# Guest tests translated from the `test "..."` blocks of
# zig/src/sexpr/parser.zig. The Zig `std.testing.allocator` leak checks have no
# analogue (values are reference counted); the fuzz test becomes a deterministic
# generator loop plus a property test.
import byte_builder
import sexpr_ast as ast
import sexpr_parser as parser

# Parse or fail the test with the error name in the message.
func parse_ok(source: bytes) -> ast.Node[]:
    match parser.parse(source):
        case Ok(nodes):
            return nodes
        case Err(_):
            assert False, "parse failed"
            return []


func children_of(n: ast.Node) -> ast.Node[]:
    match ast.as_list(n):
        case Some(children):
            return children
        case None:
            assert False, "expected a list node"
            return []


func num(n: ast.Node) -> float:
    match ast.as_number(n):
        case Some(v):
            return v
        case None:
            assert False, "expected a numeric node"
            return 0.0


func rel_close(want: float, got: float, tol: float) -> bool:
    return abs(want - got) <= tol * abs(want)


func atom_of(n: ast.Node) -> bytes:
    match ast.as_atom(n):
        case Some(a):
            return a
        case None:
            assert False, "expected an atom"
            return b""


func string_of(n: ast.Node) -> bytes:
    match ast.as_string(n):
        case Some(s):
            return s
        case None:
            assert False, "expected a string"
            return b""


# test "parse simple list"
public func test_parse_simple_list() -> bool:
    mut nodes = parse_ok(b"(hello 42 \"world\")")
    assert len(nodes) == 1, "one top-level node"
    mut children = children_of(nodes[0])
    assert len(children) == 3, "three children"
    assert atom_of(children[0]) == b"hello", "head atom"
    assert num(children[1]) == 42.0, "int child"
    assert string_of(children[2]) == b"world", "string child"
    return True

public func test_parse_nested_lists() -> bool:

    assert len(children_of(children[1])) == 2, "inner1 length"
    assert len(children_of(children[2])) == 2, "inner2 length"
    return True


# test "parse numbers and units"
public func test_parse_numbers_and_units() -> bool:
    mut nodes = parse_ok(b"(pos 1.0mm 0.5mm 10mil)")

    assert abs(1.0 - num(children[1])) <= 0.001, "1.0mm"
    assert abs(0.5 - num(children[2])) <= 0.001, "0.5mm"
    assert abs(0.254 - num(children[3])) <= 0.001, "10mil"
    return True


# test "parse si scaled values"
public func test_parse_si_scaled_values() -> bool:
    mut nodes = parse_ok(b"(vals 220k 4.7k 1M 2G 10u 100n 22p 100nF 1uH 10mA 100mV 3.3V 0.5A 47R)")
    mut c = children_of(nodes[0])
    assert rel_close(220000.0, num(c[1]), 1e-12), "220k"
    assert rel_close(4700.0, num(c[2]), 1e-12), "4.7k"
    assert rel_close(1e6, num(c[3]), 1e-12), "1M"
    assert rel_close(2e9, num(c[4]), 1e-12), "2G"
    assert rel_close(1e-5, num(c[5]), 1e-12), "10u"
    assert rel_close(1e-7, num(c[6]), 1e-12), "100n"
    assert rel_close(22e-12, num(c[7]), 1e-12), "22p"
    # 100nF == 100n: the unit letter carries no scale
    assert rel_close(1e-7, num(c[8]), 1e-12), "100nF"
    assert rel_close(1e-6, num(c[9]), 1e-12), "1uH"
    assert rel_close(0.01, num(c[10]), 1e-12), "10mA"
    assert rel_close(0.1, num(c[11]), 1e-12), "100mV"
    assert rel_close(3.3, num(c[12]), 1e-12), "3.3V"
    assert rel_close(0.5, num(c[13]), 1e-12), "0.5A"
    assert rel_close(47.0, num(c[14]), 1e-12), "47R"
    return True


# test "suffixed literals retain their spelling"
public func test_suffixed_literals_retain_their_spelling() -> bool:
    mut nodes = parse_ok(b"(vals 100nF 4.7k 33R 10uH 10% 100 2.5 3mm)")
    mut c = children_of(nodes[0])
    mut expected: bytes?[] = [None, Some(b"100nF"), Some(b"4.7k"), Some(b"33R"), Some(b"10uH"), Some(b"10%"), None, None, None]
    assert len(c) == len(expected), "child count"
    for i in range(len(expected)):
        match expected[i]:
            case Some(text):
                match ast.value_text(c[i]):
                    case Some(v):
                        assert v == text, "value_text"
                    case None:
                        assert False, "value_text missing"
                match c[i].literal:
                    case Some(l):
                        assert l == text, "literal"
                    case None:
                        assert False, "literal missing"
            case None:
                assert c[i].literal is None, "literal must be None"
    # The percent sign carries no scale: `10%` is the number 10.
    assert rel_close(10.0, num(c[5]), 1e-12), "10%"
    assert rel_close(1e-7, num(c[1]), 1e-12), "100nF"
    return True

# test "parse rejects excessively deep nesting"
public func test_parse_rejects_excessively_deep_nesting() -> bool:
    # MAX_PARSE_DEPTH + a margin of open parens: deep enough to trip the guard.
    mut depth = parser.MAX_PARSE_DEPTH + 16
    mut b = byte_builder.create()
    for _ in range(depth):
        _ = byte_builder.append_byte(mut b, ord("("))
    mut src = byte_builder.finish(b)
    match parser.parse(src):
        case Err(e):
            assert e == parser.ParseError.too_deep, "expected TooDeep"
        case Ok(_):
            assert False, "expected TooDeep, parse succeeded"
    return True


# test "parseDiag locates a mid-file syntax error"
public func test_parsediag_locates_a_mid_file_syntax_error() -> bool:
    mut diag = parser.new_diagnostic()
    # The top form closes on line 3 (first ')'), leaving a stray ')' at 3:4.
    match parser.parse_diag(b"(a\n  (b c)\n  ))", mut diag):
        case Err(e):
            assert e == parser.ParseError.unexpected_rparen, "expected UnexpectedRparen"
        case Ok(_):
            assert False, "expected an error"
    assert diag.span.line == 3, "diag line"
    assert diag.span.col == 4, "diag col"
    assert len(diag.message) > 0, "diag message"
    return True


# test "parseDiag column aligns a caret under the offending token"
public func test_parsediag_column_aligns_a_caret_under_the_offending_token() -> bool:
    mut diag = parser.new_diagnostic()
    mut line = b"(bad ]x)"
    match parser.parse_diag(line, mut diag):
        case Err(e):
            assert e == parser.ParseError.unexpected_character, "expected UnexpectedCharacter"
        case Ok(_):
            assert False, "expected an error"
    assert diag.span.line == 1, "diag line"
    assert diag.span.col == 6, "diag col"
    # Build the caret the diag renderer would: (col-1) spaces then '^'.
    mut n = diag.span.col - 1
    mut caret: int[] = []
    for _ in range(n):
        caret.append(ord(" "))
    caret.append(ord("^"))
    # The caret lands exactly on the offending ']'.
    assert line[n] == ord("]"), "caret column"
    assert bytes(caret) == b"     ^", "caret text"
    return True


# test "parseDiag points an unterminated list at its open paren"
public func test_parsediag_points_an_unterminated_list_at_its_open_paren() -> bool:
    mut diag = parser.new_diagnostic()
    match parser.parse_diag(b"(outer\n  (inner 1 2\n", mut diag):
        case Err(e):

        case Ok(_):
            assert False, "expected an error"
    # Reported at the inner '(' (2:3), the innermost list left unclosed.
    assert diag.span.line == 2, "diag line"

    return True


func fuzz_corpus() -> bytes[]:
    return [b"(design-block \"X\" (instance \"R1\" (res-0402 \"10k\") (pin 1 \"A\") (pin 2 \"B\")))", b"(net \"VIN\" (pin \"U1\" 6) (pin \"C1\" 1))", b"(pad 1 smd rect (pos -1.25 1.75) (size 0.7 0.3))", b"(vals 220k 4.7k 1M 100nF 3.3V 10mA 1.0mm 10mil 42 -5 3.3)", b"(a (b (c (d (e (f))))))", b"; comment\n(after \"comment\")\n", b"(unterminated", b")", b"\"oops", b"(bad ]char)"]


# One fuzz iteration: arbitrary bytes must never crash; every input either
# parses or returns a ParseError.
func fuzz_parse(input: bytes) -> bool:
    match parser.parse(input):
        case Ok(_):
            return True
        case Err(_):
            return True


# test "fuzz: parser never crashes on arbitrary bytes"
# Deterministic stand-in for std.testing.fuzz: the seed corpus, every prefix of
# it, and 2000 pseudo-random byte strings (LCG, biased toward the s-expression
# alphabet so that lists, strings, numbers and comments all get exercised).
public func test_fuzz_parser_never_crashes_on_arbitrary_bytes() -> bool:
    mut alphabet = b"()()\"\\; \n\t-+.0123456789abcxyzkmMuVFAHR%$,?]"
    for seed_text in fuzz_corpus():
        assert fuzz_parse(seed_text), "corpus entry"
        for cut in range(len(seed_text) + 1):
            assert fuzz_parse(seed_text[0:cut]), "corpus prefix"
    mut state = 12345
    for _round in range(2000):
        state = (state * 1103515245 + 12345) % 2147483648
        mut length = (state // 65536) % 96
        mut buf: int[] = []
        for _ in range(length):
            state = (state * 1103515245 + 12345) % 2147483648
            mut pick = (state // 65536) % 100
            if pick < 85:
                buf.append(alphabet[(state // 256) % len(alphabet)])
            else:
                buf.append((state // 256) % 256)
        assert fuzz_parse(bytes(buf)), "random input"
    return True


# The same property as mylang's own generated-input property test (100 runs).
public func test_fuzz_parser_property(data: bytes) -> bool:
    return fuzz_parse(data)

# Fetch the next token; a lexer error becomes an ERROR marker token so the
# calling test fails on its tag/text assertion instead of trapping.
func next_tok(mut t: tk.Tokenizer) -> tk.Token:
    match tk.next(mut t):
        case Ok(token):
            return token
        case Err(_):
            return tk.Token(tag=tk.TokenTag.eof, text=b"<lex error>", span=tk.tokenizer_init(b"").cur.error_span)


func expect(mut t: tk.Tokenizer, tag: tk.TokenTag, text: bytes):
    mut got = next_tok(mut t)
    assert got.tag == tag, "token tag mismatch"
    assert got.text == text, "token text mismatch"


func expect_tag(mut t: tk.Tokenizer, tag: tk.TokenTag):
    mut got = next_tok(mut t)
    assert got.tag == tag, "token tag mismatch"

    expect(mut t, tk.TokenTag.atom, b"hello")
    return True


# test "tokenize operators"
public func test_tokenize_operators() -> bool:
    mut t = tk.tokenizer_init(b"(+ a (* b c))")
    expect_tag(mut t, tk.TokenTag.lparen)
    expect(mut t, tk.TokenTag.atom, b"+")
    expect_tag(mut t, tk.TokenTag.atom)
    expect_tag(mut t, tk.TokenTag.lparen)
    mut got = next_tok(mut t)
    assert got.text == b"*", "expected the * operator"
    return True


# test "tokenize comparison operators"
public func test_tokenize_comparison_operators() -> bool:
    mut t = tk.tokenizer_init(b">= <= == !=")
    assert next_tok(mut t).text == b">=", "expected >="
    assert next_tok(mut t).text == b"<=", "expected <="
    assert next_tok(mut t).text == b"==", "expected =="
    assert next_tok(mut t).text == b"!=", "expected !="
    return True


# test "records unexpected-character error span"
public func test_records_unexpected_character_error_span() -> bool:
    mut t = tk.tokenizer_init(b"ab ?")
    expect_tag(mut t, tk.TokenTag.atom)
    match tk.next(mut t):
        case Err(e):
            assert e == tk.LexError.unexpected_character, "expected UnexpectedCharacter"
        case Ok(_):
            assert False, "expected a lex error"
    # `?` is at line 1, col 4 (a=1, b=2, space=3, ?=4).
    assert t.cur.error_span.line == 1, "error line"
    assert t.cur.error_span.col == 4, "error col"
    assert t.cur.error_span.offset == 3, "error offset"
    return True


# test "records unterminated-string error span"
public func test_records_unterminated_string_error_span() -> bool:
    mut t = tk.tokenizer_init(b"(a \"oops")
    expect_tag(mut t, tk.TokenTag.lparen)
    expect_tag(mut t, tk.TokenTag.atom)
    match tk.next(mut t):
        case Err(e):
            assert e == tk.LexError.unterminated_string, "expected UnterminatedString"
        case Ok(_):
            assert False, "expected a lex error"
    # Points at the opening quote (col 4), not the EOF where scanning stopped.
    assert t.cur.error_span.line == 1, "error line"
    assert t.cur.error_span.col == 4, "error col"
    return True


# test "tracks line and column"
public func test_tracks_line_and_column() -> bool:
    mut t = tk.tokenizer_init(b"(a\n  b)")
    mut t1 = next_tok(mut t)
    assert t1.span.line == 1, "line of ("
    assert t1.span.col == 1, "col of ("
    expect_tag(mut t, tk.TokenTag.atom)
    mut t3 = next_tok(mut t)
    assert t3.span.line == 2, "line of b"
    assert t3.span.col == 3, "col of b"
    return True

# CRC-32 (IEEE 802.3, reflected, polynomial 0xEDB88320), the counterpart of
# `std.hash.Crc32` and of Python's `zlib.crc32`.
#
#     crc32(data)                       # `Crc32.hash(data)`
#     crc32_update(crc32(a), b)         # == crc32(a + b): `Crc32.init()`, `update(a)`,
#                                       # `update(b)`, `final()` -- the running value is
#                                       # the finished checksum, as in zlib
#
# Bitwise (eight steps a byte, no table): the slice checksums short texts and small
# archive members. Values are `int` in 0..4294967295; `{x:0>8}` is
# `support_strs.hex_pad(value, 8)`.
# Polynomial 0xEDB88320 in decimal (mylang has no `0x` literals).
public const crc32_poly: int = 3988292384


# 0xFFFFFFFF.
public const crc32_mask: int = 4294967295


# Fold `data` into `crc`, a checksum already finished (0 for none).
public func crc32_update(crc: int, data: bytes) -> int:
    mut state = bit_xor(crc, crc32_mask)
    for byte in data:
        state = bit_xor(state, byte)
        mut step = 0
        while step < 8:
            if bit_and(state, 1) == 1:
                state = bit_xor(shift_right(state, 1), crc32_poly)
            else:
                state = shift_right(state, 1)
            step += 1
    return bit_xor(state, crc32_mask)


# `Crc32.hash`: the checksum of `data`.
public func crc32(data: bytes) -> int:
    return crc32_update(0, data)

# Test assertions for the port (Zig `std.testing.expect*`).
#
# A mylang test is a `public def test_*() -> bool`; the run stops at the first
# `return False`.  These helpers print what differed to a Stream and return a
# bool, so a test reads
#
#     def test_x(out: Stream) -> bool:
#         if not ex.eq_int(out, "count", got, 3):
#             return False
#
# (`ex` = `import support_expect as ex`).  `label` names the value in the message.
public func ok(out: Stream, label: str, cond: bool) -> bool:
    if not cond:
        out.print(f"expected {label.copy()} to hold")
    return cond


public func eq_int(out: Stream, label: str, got: int, want: int) -> bool:
    if got != want:
        out.print(f"{label.copy()}: got {got}, want {want}")
        return False
    return True


public func eq_str(out: Stream, label: str, got: str, want: str) -> bool:
    if got != want:
        out.print(f"{label.copy()}: got {got.copy()}, want {want.copy()}")
        return False
    return True


# Byte-exact comparison; reports the first differing offset, not two large blobs.
public func eq_bytes(out: Stream, label: str, got: bytes, want: bytes) -> bool:
    if got == want:
        return True
    mut n = min(len(got), len(want))
    mut i = 0
    while i < n and got[i] == want[i]:
        i = i + 1
    out.print(f"{label.copy()}: bytes differ at offset {i} (got {len(got)} bytes, want {len(want)} bytes)")
    return False


# Float equality within `tol` (Zig `expectApproxEqAbs`).
public func near(out: Stream, label: str, got: float, want: float, tol: float) -> bool:
    if abs(got - want) > tol:
        out.print(f"{label.copy()}: got {got}, want {want} (tolerance {tol})")
        return False
    return True


public func eq_strs(out: Stream, label: str, got: str[], want: str[]) -> bool:
    if got != want:
        out.print(f"{label.copy()}: got {got}, want {want}")
        return False
    return True

# Zig float formatting for the ported writers (no Zig counterpart file).
#
# Zig's `{d}` prints the shortest round-trip digits in plain notation and drops
# the ".0" of an integral value.  Zig's `{d:.N}` takes those same shortest
# digits and rounds half up at the Nth decimal, looking only at the first
# dropped digit (reference: `round()` in zig/lib/std/fmt/float.zig).  mylang's
# `str(float)` already yields the shortest digits in plain notation with a
# trailing ".0" on integral values, "-0.0", "inf" and "nan", so both formats are
# string surgery on `str(x)`.  Verified against 300,012 values printed by the pinned
# Zig toolchain, `{d}` and `{d:.N}` for N = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6: 0 mismatches
# (`python3 mylang/tools/float_fmt_verify.py`).
#
# `strings.format_float(x, n)` is NOT a substitute: it rounds the exact binary
# value, which is what Go and Rust do and what PORTING.md warns about.
# Zig `{d}`.
public func fmt_float(x: float) -> str:
    mut text = str(x)
    if text.endswith(".0"):
        return text[:len(text) - 2]
    return text


# Add one to a string of decimal digits; may grow it by one digit ("99" -> "100").
func add_one(digits: str) -> str:
    mut ds = [for c in digits yield ord(c) - 48]
    mut i = len(ds) - 1
    mut carry = True
    while carry and i >= 0:
        if ds[i] == 9:
            ds[i] = 0
            i = i - 1
        else:
            ds[i] = ds[i] + 1
            carry = False
    mut text = "".join([for d in ds yield chr(48 + d)])
    if carry:
        return "1" + text
    return text


# Zig `{d:.N}`.
public func fmt_float_prec(x: float, n: int) -> str:
    mut text = str(x)
    if text == "inf" or text == "-inf" or text == "nan":
        return text
    mut negative = text.startswith("-")
    if negative:
        text = text[1:]
    mut dot = text.find(".")
    mut whole = text[:dot]
    mut frac = text[dot + 1:]
    if len(frac) > n:
        mut round_up = ord(frac[n]) >= 53
        mut digits = whole + frac[:n]
        if round_up:
            digits = add_one(digits)
        whole = digits[:len(digits) - n]
        frac = digits[len(digits) - n:]
    else:
        while len(frac) < n:
            frac = frac + "0"
    mut out = whole
    if n > 0:
        out = out + "." + frac
    if negative:
        out = "-" + out
    return out

# Zig-compatible number parsing: `std.fmt.parseInt(T, s, 10)` and
# `std.fmt.parseFloat(f64, s)`, each as an Option (Zig's `catch null`).
#
# mylang's `int(s)` and `float(s)` agree with Zig on everything the exporter
# feeds them (sign, leading zeros, `_` between digits, `.5`, `5.`, exponents,
# `inf`/`nan`, out-of-range -> None for int and +-inf for float), with two
# differences that these wrappers remove:
#
#   * `int(" 5")`, `int("5 ")` and `float(" 1")` succeed (surrounding whitespace is
#     trimmed, as in Python); Zig rejects them with InvalidCharacter.
#   * `float("0x1p3")` / `float("0x10")` (hex floats) are None; Zig accepts them.
#     Nothing in the slice can reach a hex float (the tokenizer classifies
#     numbers first), so they stay None.
#
# Verified against `zig run` (0.17.0-dev.1683) on 23 integer and 39 float spellings.
# True when the first or last character could only be trimmed whitespace (or any
# non-printable/non-ASCII character), which no valid Zig number has at its edges.
func has_edge_junk(s: str) -> bool:
    if len(s) == 0:
        return False
    mut first = ord(s[0])
    mut last = ord(s[len(s) - 1])
    return first <= 32 or first > 126 or last <= 32 or last > 126


# Zig `std.fmt.parseInt(i64, s, 10) catch null`.
public func parse_int(s: str) -> int?:
    if has_edge_junk(s):
        return None
    return s.parse_int()


# Zig `std.fmt.parseInt(u32, s, 10) catch null` (a value outside 0..4294967295 is None).
public func parse_u32(s: str) -> int?:
    mut v = parse_int(s)
    if v is None:
        return None
    if v < 0 or v > 4294967295:
        return None
    return Some(v)


# Zig `std.fmt.parseFloat(f64, s) catch null` (hex floats excepted, see above).
public func parse_float(s: str) -> float?:
    if has_edge_junk(s):
        return None
    return s.parse_float()

# SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4), the counterpart of `std.crypto.hash.sha2.Sha256`.
#
#     digest = support_sha256.sha256(data)       # 32 bytes, `Sha256.hash(data, &out, .{})`
#
# Zig's incremental `init` / `update` / `update` / `finalResult` is the digest of the
# concatenation: collect the pieces (`data_a + data_b`, or a `byte_builder`) and hash once.
# All arithmetic is `u32` with `wrapping_add` and the bit helpers, so the code reads like the
# specification; a full 64-byte block is read straight from `data`, only the padded tail
# is copied. Verified against Python's `hashlib` on the boundary lengths in the test file.
# The 64 round constants K[0..63] of FIPS 180-4 in decimal (mylang has no `0x` literals),
# as a function (D6: a table constant is a function).
func round_constants() -> u32[]:
    return [1116352408, 1899447441, 3049323471, 3921009573, 961987163, 1508970993, 2453635748, 2870763221, 3624381080, 310598401, 607225278, 1426881987, 1925078388, 2162078206, 2614888103, 3248222580, 3835390401, 4022224774, 264347078, 604807628, 770255983, 1249150122, 1555081692, 1996064986, 2554220882, 2821834349, 2952996808, 3210313671, 3336571891, 3584528711, 113926993, 338241895, 666307205, 773529912, 1294757372, 1396182291, 1695183700, 1986661051, 2177026350, 2456956037, 2730485921, 2820302411, 3259730800, 3345764771, 3516065817, 3600352804, 4094571909, 275423344, 430227734, 506948616, 659060556, 883997877, 958139571, 1322822218, 1537002063, 1747873779, 1955562222, 2024104815, 2227730452, 2361852424, 2428436474, 2756734187, 3204031479, 3329325298]


func rotr(x: u32, n: u32) -> u32:
    return bit_or(shift_right(x, n), shift_left(x, 32u32 - n))


# One 64-byte block of `data` starting at `off` folded into `state` (8 words).
func compress(mut state: u32[], data: bytes, off: int, k: u32[]):
    mut w: u32[] = []
    mut i = 0
    while i < 16:
        mut p = off + 4 * i
        mut word = shift_left(u32(data[p]), 24u32)
        word = bit_or(word, shift_left(u32(data[p + 1]), 16u32))
        word = bit_or(word, shift_left(u32(data[p + 2]), 8u32))
        word = bit_or(word, u32(data[p + 3]))
        w.append(word)
        i += 1
    while i < 64:
        mut x = w[i - 15]
        mut y = w[i - 2]
        mut s0 = bit_xor(bit_xor(rotr(x, 7u32), rotr(x, 18u32)), shift_right(x, 3u32))
        mut s1 = bit_xor(bit_xor(rotr(y, 17u32), rotr(y, 19u32)), shift_right(y, 10u32))
        w.append(wrapping_add(wrapping_add(w[i - 16], s0), wrapping_add(w[i - 7], s1)))
        i += 1
    mut a = state[0]
    mut b = state[1]
    mut c = state[2]
    mut d = state[3]
    mut e = state[4]
    mut f = state[5]
    mut g = state[6]
    mut h = state[7]
    i = 0
    while i < 64:
        mut big1 = bit_xor(bit_xor(rotr(e, 6u32), rotr(e, 11u32)), rotr(e, 25u32))
        mut ch = bit_xor(bit_and(e, f), bit_and(bit_xor(e, 4294967295u32), g))
        mut t1 = wrapping_add(wrapping_add(h, big1), wrapping_add(wrapping_add(ch, k[i]), w[i]))
        mut big0 = bit_xor(bit_xor(rotr(a, 2u32), rotr(a, 13u32)), rotr(a, 22u32))
        mut maj = bit_xor(bit_xor(bit_and(a, b), bit_and(a, c)), bit_and(b, c))
        mut t2 = wrapping_add(big0, maj)
        h = g
        g = f
        f = e
        e = wrapping_add(d, t1)
        d = c
        c = b
        b = a
        a = wrapping_add(t1, t2)
        i += 1
    state[0] = wrapping_add(state[0], a)
    state[1] = wrapping_add(state[1], b)
    state[2] = wrapping_add(state[2], c)
    state[3] = wrapping_add(state[3], d)
    state[4] = wrapping_add(state[4], e)
    state[5] = wrapping_add(state[5], f)
    state[6] = wrapping_add(state[6], g)
    state[7] = wrapping_add(state[7], h)


# The last one or two blocks: the tail of `data` after its full blocks, a 128 byte,
# zeros, and the message length in bits as eight big-endian bytes.
func padded_tail(data: bytes, full: int) -> bytes:
    mut tail = data[full * 64:].to_list()
    tail.append(128)
    while len(tail) % 64 != 56:
        tail.append(0)
    mut bits = len(data) * 8
    mut shift = 56
    while shift >= 0:
        tail.append(bit_and(shift_right(bits, shift), 255))
        shift -= 8
    return bytes(tail)


# `Sha256.hash`: the 32-byte digest of `data`.
public func sha256(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    mut k = round_constants()
    # H0..H7 of FIPS 180-4 (0x6a09e667, 0xbb67ae85, 0x3c6ef372, 0xa54ff53a, 0x510e527f,
    # 0x9b05688c, 0x1f83d9ab, 0x5be0cd19) in decimal.
    mut state: u32[] = [1779033703, 3144134277, 1013904242, 2773480762, 1359893119, 2600822924, 528734635, 1541459225]
    mut full = len(data) // 64
    mut off = 0
    while off < full * 64:
        compress(mut state, data, off, k)
        off += 64
    mut tail = padded_tail(data, full)
    off = 0
    while off < len(tail):
        compress(mut state, tail, off, k)
        off += 64
    mut out: int[] = []
    for word in state:
        out.append(int(shift_right(word, 24u32)))
        out.append(int(bit_and(shift_right(word, 16u32), 255u32)))
        out.append(int(bit_and(shift_right(word, 8u32), 255u32)))
        out.append(int(bit_and(word, 255u32)))
    return bytes(out)

# Stable sorting with a comparator, the counterpart of Zig's `std.mem.sort`.
#
# `std.mem.sort(T, items, ctx, lessThan)` is stable and sorts in place; the two
# functions below do the same for a `list[T]` held by the caller:
#
#     support_sort.sort_by(mut pins, pin_less)              # lessThan(a, b)
#     support_sort.sort_by_ctx(mut ids, cands, cand_less)   # lessThan(ctx, a, b)
#
# `less(a, b)` must be a strict weak order ("a sorts strictly before b"), as in
# Zig; elements that compare equal keep their input order.  mylang has no
# closures, so a Zig comparator that reads `ctx` receives it as an explicit first
# argument (`sort_by_ctx`).  When a comparator is only "field ascending" (or
# ascending on a tuple of fields), `xs.sort(key=lambda p: (p.x, p.y))` is shorter
# and equally stable; use these when the order needs a descending string, a
# custom string comparison, or context.
# `min` is not visible inside a generic function on the pinned compiler
# (E_UNKNOWN_SYMBOL), so the two bounds go through this plain helper.
func lower(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    if a < b:
        return a
    return b


# Merge the sorted halves items[lo:mid] and items[mid:hi] through `tmp`.
func merge_run[T](mut items: T[], mut tmp: T[], lo: int, mid: int, hi: int, less: func(T, T) -> bool):
    mut i = lo
    mut j = mid
    mut k = lo
    while i < mid and j < hi:
        # take from the right run only when it is strictly smaller: keeps stability
        if less(items[j], items[i]):
            tmp[k] = items[j].copy()
            j = j + 1
        else:
            tmp[k] = items[i].copy()
            i = i + 1
        k = k + 1
    while i < mid:
        tmp[k] = items[i].copy()
        i = i + 1
        k = k + 1
    while j < hi:
        tmp[k] = items[j].copy()
        j = j + 1
        k = k + 1
    k = lo
    while k < hi:
        items[k] = tmp[k].copy()
        k = k + 1


# Sort `items` in place, stably, by `less` (Zig `std.mem.sort(T, items, {}, less)`).
public func sort_by[T](mut items: T[], less: func(T, T) -> bool):
    mut n = len(items)
    if n < 2:
        return
    mut tmp = items.copy()
    mut width = 1
    while width < n:
        mut lo = 0
        while lo < n:
            mut mid = lower(lo + width, n)
            mut hi = lower(lo + 2 * width, n)
            if mid < hi:
                merge_run(mut items, mut tmp, lo, mid, hi, less)
            lo = lo + 2 * width
        width = width * 2


# Sort `ids` in place, stably, by `less(ctx, a, b)` (Zig `std.mem.sort(T, items, ctx, less)`).
public func sort_by_ctx[T, C](mut items: T[], ctx: C, less: func(C, T, T) -> bool):
    # Sort a permutation of indexes with the ctx-free merge, then apply it.
    mut n = len(items)
    if n < 2:
        return
    mut order = [for k in range(n) yield k]
    mut snapshot = items.copy()
    sort_indexes(mut order, snapshot, ctx, less)
    mut k = 0
    while k < n:
        items[k] = snapshot[order[k]].copy()
        k = k + 1


func merge_index_run[T, C](mut order: int[], mut tmp: int[], snapshot: T[], ctx: C, span: int[], less: func(C, T, T) -> bool):
    mut lo = span[0]
    mut mid = span[1]
    mut hi = span[2]
    mut i = lo
    mut j = mid
    mut k = lo
    while i < mid and j < hi:
        if less(ctx, snapshot[order[j]], snapshot[order[i]]):
            tmp[k] = order[j]
            j = j + 1
        else:
            tmp[k] = order[i]
            i = i + 1
        k = k + 1
    while i < mid:
        tmp[k] = order[i]
        i = i + 1
        k = k + 1
    while j < hi:
        tmp[k] = order[j]
        j = j + 1
        k = k + 1
    k = lo
    while k < hi:
        order[k] = tmp[k]
        k = k + 1


func sort_indexes[T, C](mut order: int[], snapshot: T[], ctx: C, less: func(C, T, T) -> bool):
    mut n = len(order)
    mut tmp = order.copy()
    mut width = 1
    while width < n:
        mut lo = 0
        while lo < n:
            mut mid = lower(lo + width, n)
            mut hi = lower(lo + 2 * width, n)
            if mid < hi:
                merge_index_run(mut order, mut tmp, snapshot, ctx, [lo, mid, hi], less)
            lo = lo + 2 * width
        width = width * 2

import support_sort as ss

record Item:
    key: int
    tag: int


func item_less(a: Item, b: Item) -> bool:
    return a.key < b.key


func item_greater(a: Item, b: Item) -> bool:
    return a.key > b.key


func by_rank(ranks: int[], a: Item, b: Item) -> bool:
    return ranks[a.key] < ranks[b.key]


func make_items(n: int, modulus: int, seed: int) -> Item[]:
    mut items: Item[] = []
    mut state = seed
    mut i = 0
    while i < n:
        state = (state * 1103515245 + 12345) % 2147483648
        items.append(Item(key=state // 65536 % modulus, tag=i))
        i = i + 1
    return items


func tags(items: Item[]) -> int[]:
    return [for it in items yield it.tag]


public func test_sort_by_is_stable_and_matches_the_keyed_sort() -> bool:
    mut n = 0
    while n < 40:
        mut items = make_items(n, 5, n + 7)
        mut want = sorted(items, key=lambda it: it.key)
        ss.sort_by(mut items, item_less)
        if tags(items) != tags(want):
            return False
        n = n + 1
    return True


public func test_sort_by_descending_keeps_input_order_of_equal_keys() -> bool:
    mut items = [Item(key=1, tag=0), Item(key=2, tag=1), Item(key=1, tag=2), Item(key=2, tag=3), Item(key=0, tag=4)]
    ss.sort_by(mut items, item_greater)
    return tags(items) == [1, 3, 0, 2, 4]


public func test_sort_by_ctx_reads_the_context_and_is_stable() -> bool:
    mut ranks = [3, 0, 2, 1, 2]
    mut items = [for k in [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 2, 1]yield Item(key=k, tag=k * 10)]
    ss.sort_by_ctx(mut items, ranks, by_rank)
    return tags(items) == [10, 10, 30, 20, 40, 20, 0]


public func test_sort_by_handles_empty_and_single_lists() -> bool:
    mut empty: Item[] = []
    ss.sort_by(mut empty, item_less)
    mut one = [Item(key=1, tag=9)]
    ss.sort_by(mut one, item_less)
    return len(empty) == 0 and tags(one) == [9]

# Port of zig/src/uuid.zig: the canonical UUID text form, written in one place.
# Stamps the RFC 4122 version nibble and variant bits and renders the 8-4-4-4-12
# lowercase hex text.
# Which UUID this is. The Zig enum's value is the version nibble already
# shifted into the high half of byte 6; `version_bits` recovers it.
public enum Version:
    random_v4
    name_v5


public func version_bits(version: Version) -> int:
    match version:
        case Version.random_v4:
            return 64
        case Version.name_v5:
            return 80


# Length of the canonical text form: 32 hex digits and 4 dashes.
public const TEXT_LEN: int = 36


# Stamp `raw`'s (16 bytes) version and variant fields and render the canonical
# `xxxxxxxx-xxxx-Vxxx-yxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx` text.
public func format(raw: bytes, version: Version) -> bytes:
    mut b = raw.to_list()
    b[6] = bit_or(bit_and(b[6], 15), version_bits(version))
    b[8] = bit_or(bit_and(b[8], 63), 128)
    mut h = bytes(b).hex()
    return (h[0:8] + "-" + h[8:12] + "-" + h[12:16] + "-" + h[16:20] + "-" + h[20:32]).encode()

# Guest test translated from the `test "..."` block of zig/src/uuid.zig.
import uuid

# test "format stamps version and variant and renders the canonical shape"
public func test_format_stamps_version_and_variant_and_renders_the_canonical_shape() -> bool:
    mut raw_list = [for i in range(16) yield i]
    mut raw = bytes(raw_list)
    mut v4 = uuid.format(raw, uuid.Version.random_v4)
    assert v4 == b"00010203-0405-4607-8809-0a0b0c0d0e0f", "v4 text"
    mut v5 = uuid.format(raw, uuid.Version.name_v5)
    assert v5 == b"00010203-0405-5607-8809-0a0b0c0d0e0f", "v5 text"
    assert len(v4) == uuid.TEXT_LEN, "text length"

import byte_builder
import support_crc32 as crc_mod

public record Entry:
    name: bytes
    data: bytes


public const err_zip32_limit_exceeded: str = "Zip32LimitExceeded"


public func encoded_size(entries: Entry[]) -> Result[int, str]:
    if len(entries) > 65535:
        return Err(err_zip32_limit_exceeded)
    mut local_size = 0
    mut central_size = 0
    for entry in entries:
        if len(entry.name) > 65535 or len(entry.data) > 4294967295:
            return Err(err_zip32_limit_exceeded)
        local_size += 30 + len(entry.name) + len(entry.data)
        central_size += 46 + len(entry.name)
        if local_size > 4294967295 or central_size > 4294967295:
            return Err(err_zip32_limit_exceeded)
    return Ok(local_size + central_size + 22)


public func write(mut w: byte_builder.Builder, entries: Entry[]) -> Result[Unit, str]:
    match encoded_size(entries):
        case Err(_):
            return Err("WriteFailed")
        case Ok(_):
            pass
    mut offset = 0
    # Local file headers and stored data, in the supplied order.
    for entry in entries:
        mut crc = crc_mod.crc32(entry.data)
        byte_builder.append(mut w, b"PK\x03\x04")
        write_int(mut w, 20, 2)
        write_int(mut w, 0, 2)
        write_int(mut w, 0, 2)
        write_int(mut w, 0, 2)
        write_int(mut w, 33, 2) # 0x0021: 1980-01-01.
        write_int(mut w, crc, 4)
        write_int(mut w, len(entry.data), 4)
        write_int(mut w, len(entry.data), 4)
        write_int(mut w, len(entry.name), 2)
        write_int(mut w, 0, 2)
        byte_builder.append(mut w, entry.name)
        byte_builder.append(mut w, entry.data)
        offset += 30 + len(entry.name) + len(entry.data)
    mut cd_start = offset
    mut cd_size = 0
    mut local_off = 0
    # Central directory.
    for entry2 in entries:
        mut crc2 = crc_mod.crc32(entry2.data)
        byte_builder.append(mut w, b"PK\x01\x02")
        write_int(mut w, 20, 2)
        write_int(mut w, 20, 2)
        write_int(mut w, 0, 2)
        write_int(mut w, 0, 2)
        write_int(mut w, 0, 2)
        write_int(mut w, 33, 2)
        write_int(mut w, crc2, 4)
        write_int(mut w, len(entry2.data), 4)
        write_int(mut w, len(entry2.data), 4)
        write_int(mut w, len(entry2.name), 2)
        write_int(mut w, 0, 2)
        write_int(mut w, 0, 2)
        write_int(mut w, 0, 2)
        write_int(mut w, 0, 2)
        write_int(mut w, 0, 4)
        write_int(mut w, local_off, 4)
        byte_builder.append(mut w, entry2.name)
        cd_size += 46 + len(entry2.name)
        local_off += 30 + len(entry2.name) + len(entry2.data)
    # End of central directory.
    byte_builder.append(mut w, b"PK\x05\x06")
    write_int(mut w, 0, 2)
    write_int(mut w, 0, 2)
    write_int(mut w, len(entries), 2)
    write_int(mut w, len(entries), 2)
    write_int(mut w, cd_size, 4)
    write_int(mut w, cd_start, 4)
    write_int(mut w, 0, 2)
    return Ok(())


func write_int(mut w: byte_builder.Builder, value: int, count: int):
    mut n = value
    mut i = 0
    while i < count:
        _ = byte_builder.append_byte(mut w, n % 256)
        n = n // 256
        i += 1
